Psych Mirror sits between Dreamer (which writes claims) and downstream consumers (context assembly, entity embeddings, Mirror UI, export). One LLM call produces all three tiers; profileCompact is a strict compression of profileText, not independently generated.

![Fig. 1 Psych Mirror agent. Claims about a Person/Facet feed a single LLM call; three tiers fan out to seven consumers — tier choice is dictated by each consumer's token budget and use case.](figures/oneiron-arch-0025-psych-mirror-v1-fig-1.png)

Fig. 1 Psych Mirror agent. Claims about a Person/Facet feed a single LLM call; three tiers fan out to seven consumers — tier choice is dictated by each consumer's token budget and use case. Amended 2026-07-02 per `ONE-LLMB`: Dreamer calls language models through a raw-call engine trait, not through an agent-loop abstraction. Durability, retries, budget policy, consent waits, and workflow branching stay above the trait; adapters only speak provider wire protocols and classify failures.

The channel itself is nothing new: the publisher is an ACTOR entity, and publisher ↔ user is a normal comm channel with that actor as counterparty. DOWN: fix notices, known-issue announcements, questions — rendered by the surface in **platform voice** (EC-7: outside the dyad, never the companion's voice; muting works, but law/store blocks stay visible). UP has three rungs by consent depth:

**The UP lane — three rungs by consent depth** The ruling (r7): compliance is vault-resident policy data, never code. The charter-compiles-to-policy pattern applied to statute — the law's text (with citation) is the source; an agent compiles it to deterministic rule rows; the dispatch gate enforces only rows. Coverage is honest: popular jurisdictions ship as seed rows, everything else is configurable, and the pack carries its warning. Laws change: updates ride the OF-401 publisher loop; any agent may propose a row amendment citing a law change — **tightening auto-applies with a notice; loosening waits for the owner's stamp**. No vendor never-loosen ceilings.

``` ascii-fig
THE LAW (real text, cited) ──agent compiles──▶ RULE ROWS (versioned data)
                                                    │
THE GATE, at dispatch:                              ▼
  comm.jurisdiction claim ──────┐      ┌─ missing List-Unsubscribe? BLOCK
  recipient legal form ─────────┤ pick │─ list provenance unknown?  BLOCK
  channel (email vs DM) ────────┘ rows └─ JP published-address needs the
  strictest wins · unknown → strict       PUBLICATION CONTEXT stored, or BLOCK
                                        ─ rule row verified_at stale? BLOCK
                                                    │
                                           all green ─▶ send fires
```

**Rule-row schema** Echo safety falls out of §3: our own writes come back in the next poll carrying UIDs we minted — passports with `direction: ours` recognize them. Two-way sync stays deliberately narrow (CalDAV, where the protocol was built for it) — the research verdict is unambiguous that promising real-time two-way across Google + Outlook + vault on day one is how calendar projects die.

The healer's trigger is the **failure ladder** (ONE-1887), which classifies a failing task before anyone reaches for repair:

**The ONE-1887 failure ladder — classification decides the response**

| Classification | Response |
|----|----|
| Transient | Bounded auto-retry — new ATTEMPTs on the same task; no healer involvement yet. |
| N consecutive failures (default 3) | Escalation; the mode is selectable, and the AUTO default is the HEALER AGENT. |
| Permanent | Healer diagnoses first, then hands to a human with the diagnosis attached. |
| Ambiguous | Straight to a human — the healer does not guess on unclassifiable failures. |

Most findings never reach a person: the healer consumes them first, repairs what it safely can, and proposes the rest — escalation to a human is the last of its four fix types. **The residue that does reach the human orders by impact, never by count**: one parked run blocking a task chain sits above fifty copies of a cosmetic complaint. Two operational laws from the core doc survive unchanged: the global render budget is a **fixed render constant, not agent state** — an agent that "maxes everything" saturates the cap, it cannot grow it (shed order: SKILLS found and AGENTS cand rows first — 2026-08-28 — then MEMORIES snippets → TASKS to counts → AGENTS to counts → WORLDS to counts; PINNED and the legend never shed). And **owner-excluded worlds are filtered before the board projection** — masked fully, no name, no count; the agent genuinely cannot know they exist, which is the intended privacy cost.

Three shape rules follow from that single cap. The memories budget is **shared across the active worlds, not allocated per world** — per-world budgets let N foreign worlds × full text starve the reasoning space. Foreign worlds therefore default to the cheapest tier, **index-only**, and are opened by verb rather than by default. And the WORLDS rows carry their own cap, overflowing to a "+N more" count rather than growing the block. The affordance map — the available-but-off rows — is a **strict subset of the allowed-set**: rendering an excluded world as "excluded" would leak both its existence and its label to a compromised agent, which is why masking is total rather than count-only. #### Implementation order > Why no “anon” actor node
>
> An explicit `anon` actor node for unattributed writes was **rejected**. Anon provenance carries zero information over absent provenance, costs a Claim entity per edge, and — fatally — would grant unattributed writes supersession rights over attributed truth: the same hole family as M4's imported→auto finding, contrary to the [ARCH-0040](/oneiron/core/oneiron-arch-0040-write-gates-provenance-trust-v1/) fail-closed posture. The pinned principle: **an unattributed write can never displace attributed truth as current state.** The session-actor ergonomics that keep this from being onerous — bind an actor once per session/handle, then write normally, with the MCP daemon injecting the session actor on the named-writes lane — live in [ARCH-0028](/oneiron/agents/oneiron-arch-0028-mcp-external-agent-surface-v1/); the surface names there (`as_actor` and the like) are implemented as engine-internal ergonomics, not pinned public ABI. The canonical snapshot is also the recovery anchor. When corruption is detected, Oneiron does not delete the bad manifest first. It quarantines it by renaming to an `.invalid-N` artifact, then rebuilds from validated canonical state. The recovery path is tiered so a localized carrier issue does not automatically become a full-vault rebuild.

**What ships when**

| Tier | Behavior |
|----|----|
| `Healthy` | Manifest and canonical state validate; normal open and maintenance paths continue. |
| `TargetedChunkRepair` | A localized carrier/manifest problem is quarantined and rebuilt from surviving canonical state. |
| `FullRebuild` | The vault window rebuilds from the canonical snapshot after the bad manifest is renamed to .invalid-N. |

If repair pressure is too high, the implementation returns typed bounded backpressure such as `OverlayLimit` rather than silently dropping obligations. Causality is not a typed edge. A causal link is an ordinary claim in a `causal.*` predicate pack — `causal.causes` for the general case, alongside the affect-side `affect.trigger` instance — so `Claim.confidence` and `Claim.source` come free and no entity type is minted for it. On such a claim the [`dr:NSD-195`](#dr:NSD-195) pre-commit topology gate asserts `cause.occurredAt ≤ effect.occurredAt` on the event-time axis, once, deterministically, at write time.

The check is **world-scoped** and never crosses a `WorldScope` boundary: real cannot cause fiction, and fiction cannot constrain real. A year-3000 roleplay typed today carries an `occurredAt` of when it was typed, so the check does not fire spuriously; a world that extracts in-narrative times is validated inside its own timeline.

A violation is never a silent delete. Cycles and orphans fail closed because they corrupt the substrate. A time-order violation is evidence instead — it feeds confidence and gate handling, conditioned on who claimed it:

**Causal time-order violation, routed by Claim.source**

| Source | What the violation means | Action |
|----|----|----|
| `user_stated` | the user asserted something time-impossible | Surface as a potential contradiction — misremembered, or in-world. The user's word is never dropped. |
| `inferred / generated` | the agent's own derivation is likely wrong | Down-weight or discard the inference; the violation lowers that claim's confidence. | stops**: a write is session-scoped iff made through the session handle. Backstops for caller mistakes: (a) the witness-door ownership check (base-path witness targeting a session-owned conversation is rejected); (b) the **taint guard** — the base batch preflight rejects any base entity/edge/claim-subject/typed-carrier referencing an id in the live-overlay taint set. Taint scope is live sessions only: after close the id names nothing; caller-retained knowledge is outside any storage seam's threat model.
- **No mutable process-shared state on session handles**: structural-kind registration refused; session-flow metrics/tracing id-only (grep-audited). - **Claim subjects keep original entity ids forever.** Provenance truth is bitemporal: the claim said B because the evidence said B. Canonicalization is a read/projection-time concern, resolved through the redirect table.
- **Aggregations re-derive.** Anything projector-written (PPR seeds, actor.\* rollups, reliability posteriors) takes the redirect table as projection input and heals on rebuild — ARCH-0035 re-derivability, no backfill migrations.

- **Facet ops touch no entity ids at all** — `facet_of` scoping only; reads are already facet-aware (ARCH-0022 null-shadow rules).
